comparison: Perfect agreement on clinical characterization (C1-C5, C27, C45, C58). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the clinical description, infection duration, treatment history, and immunocompromised status without challenge. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED.

Significant disagreement on interpretation of population structure (C6-C10, C19). OpenEval finds the spatial structure interpretation well-supported by phylogenetic and haplotype data. Peer reviewers accept the data showing clades but challenge the interpretation, questioning whether clades represent spatial subpopulations or could be genotypes in a well-mixed population (Essential revision #2). OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN.

Disagreement on regression analysis robustness (C11-C13). OpenEval finds the methodology sound with appropriate confidence intervals. Peer reviewers raise concerns about non-independence of data points and whether estimates are robust to removal of certain points (Essential revisions #5, #6). OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN.

Substantial disagreement on Ne estimate (C14-C15, C22, C39, C47). OpenEval finds the simulation analysis and inference about selection dominating drift well-supported. Peer reviewers express extensive methodological concerns about Wright-Fisher model assumptions, initial allele frequencies, recombination assumptions, and whether a single Ne is adequate (Essential revisions #2, #3b, #3c, #4). OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN.

Partial overlap on Ne limitations (C16-C18, C20). OpenEval evaluates the acknowledgment of limitations as appropriate and transparent. Peer reviewers incorporate these concerns into their broader uncertainty about the Ne estimate itself, questioning underlying assumptions more fundamentally. OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN (in context of R4).

Disagreement on selection interpretation (C21, C51-C52). OpenEval finds dN/dS data clearly supports purifying selection and lack of positive selection. Peer reviewers challenge this in context of acute infections, citing contradictory evidence from McCrone et al. 2018 and Xue & Bloom 2020 showing non-synonymous mutations dominate in acute infections (Essential revision #1). OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN.

Partial overlap on study advantages (C23-C25, C46). OpenEval finds the self-assessment of advantages (long infection, frequent sampling, reduced selection) appropriate. Peer reviewers accept these features exist but question their broader implications, particularly whether findings from chronic infections apply to acute infections. OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN (in broader context).

Disagreement on validation rigor (C26, C73-C76). OpenEval expresses concerns about methodological shortcuts (applying influenza B false positive rates to influenza A, post-hoc data exclusion). Peer reviewers do not specifically challenge these validation results and implicitly accept them. OpenEval: UNCERTAIN, Peer: SUPPORTED.

Strong disagreement on extrapolation to typical infections (C28-C30, C48). OpenEval finds the extrapolation uncertain due to simplified calculations and lack of direct data. Peer reviewers explicitly reject this extrapolation, stating it's 'not evident' that chronic infection estimates apply to acute infections and requesting title revision to focus on chronic infections (Essential revision #1). OpenEval: UNCERTAIN, Peer: UNSUPPORTED.

Agreement on theoretical logic but disagreement on practical relevance (C31-C36). OpenEval finds the chain of inference about longer infections' disproportionate influence logically sound based on population genetics theory. Peer reviewers question whether chronic infection findings are relevant to global evolution, particularly given differences between acute and chronic infections (Essential revision #1). OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN.

Agreement on literature review (C37-C38, C40-C44 vs C37-C41, C49-C50). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the characterization of prior literature and existing debates without challenge. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on technical validation (C55-C57, C64-C65). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the sequencing validation approach, replicate analysis, and frequency-dependent reliability characterization. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on modeling assumptions (C62-C63, C66-C67). OpenEval finds the assumptions about recombination, reassortment, and frequency cutoffs reasonable and transparently stated. Peer reviewers question multiple methodological choices including recombination structure assumptions, segment selection (HA/NA experience strongest selection), and generation time assumptions (Essential revisions #3c, #7, #9). OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN.

Partial overlap on bioinformatics methods (C68-C72). OpenEval finds BEAST2, HKY model, and haplotype reconstruction appropriate and standard. Peer reviewers raise concerns about some methodological choices (segment selection, recombination assumptions) that relate to the broader analysis pipeline. OpenEval: SUPPORTED, Peer: UNCERTAIN (in broader methodological context).

Agreement on background context (C49-C50). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the characterization of influenza population structure and global evolution without challenge. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on resistance mutations (C53-C54). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the observation of substitutions at resistance loci and their association with zanamivir resistance. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED.
Agreement on data availability (C59). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers accept the data availability statement without comment. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED.
